question: Does Cerezo et al. provide a reusable, site-resolved fish baseline for Buenlag-Sabangan River?

method.summary: Reviewed the journal's article page and complete four-page publisher-hosted PDF, including the abstract, methods, results and article footer. No local PDF or secondary catch tables were retained.
method.sourceScope: The paper describes fish, crustacean and mangrove-related macrofauna in the Buenlag-Sabangan River area of Barangay Buenlag, Binmaley, Pangasinan. It reports fish sampling in upstream, midstream and downstream portions but supplies no coordinates or named fish-sampling stations.
method.provenanceFinding: Fish and crustacean catch from fyke-net fishers was purchased by weight; the paper also says secondary data from previous research and the Binmaley Municipal Agriculture Office supported its primary data. The publication does not separate which fish-name labels came from which source or collection event.
method.reuseFinding: The article is freely accessible and the journal calls its archive open access, but no item-specific Creative Commons or other public reuse license was identified. The publisher site also displays a copyright form and an all-rights-reserved footer. Treat content redistribution and public-app reuse as unapproved pending clarification.

publication.title: Mangroves and associated macroflora and macrofauna of Buenlag-Sabangan River in Binmaley, Pangasinan
publication.journal: International Journal of Fauna and Biological Studies
publication.manuscriptReceived: 04-11-2017 as printed; date-order convention not specified
publication.manuscriptAccepted: 05-12-2017 as printed; date-order convention not specified
publication.citation: Cerezo, R. B., Parreno, S. C., Fernandez, J. B., & Dela Peña, R. V. (2018). Mangroves and associated macroflora and macrofauna of Buenlag-Sabangan River in Binmaley, Pangasinan. International Journal of Fauna and Biological Studies, 5(1), 15-18.
publication.accessStatus: Publisher article page and complete four-page PDF reviewed online on 2026-11-19.

studyArea.localityAsReported: River in Barangay Buenlag, Binmaley, Pangasinan
studyArea.studyLengthAndWidthAsReported: Approximately 1.83 km long and 38.78 m wide
studyArea.habitatContext: Mangrove-associated river with downstream, midstream and upstream fish sampling; the paper notes river inundation during high tide.

sampling.collectionSummary: The methods say fishers' catches were purchased, fish/crustaceans counted and identified, and species common name, scientific name, length and weight recorded. The article does not publish the separate data sheets or a species-by-net, species-by-station, or species-by-date table.
sampling.taxonomicMethodAsReported: One methods passage says specimens were identified and classified to family level, while the abstract lists binomial-form and genus-level fish names.

rights.accessStatus: The journal states that articles are freely and permanently accessible online without subscription or registration.
rights.copyrightEvidence: The publisher site displays a copyright-form link and an all-rights-reserved footer; these do not establish a license to redistribute this article's extracted content.

internalConsistency.issue: The abstract says five stations were established, while the methods refer to six fyke nets and later say four fishers with fyke nets were selected.
internalConsistency.disposition: Preserve all three source statements; do not infer a station-to-net or fisher-to-station mapping.

internalConsistency.issue: The publisher HTML abstract and PDF text extraction differ on spellings for Rhynchorhamphus/Rhynchomphus georgii, Suggrundus/Suggurundus macracanthus, and Gerres erythrourus/erythourus.
internalConsistency.disposition: Retain both source forms as variants; do not silently normalize or claim a specimen-level taxonomic identification.

internalConsistency.issue: The methods say fish were classified to family level, but the abstract presents 15 labels including binomial-form and genus-only names.
internalConsistency.disposition: Treat the 15 as publication-reported fish-name strings, not verified species determinations.

internalConsistency.issue: The publication reports purchased fisher catches and use of secondary sources, with no collection period or source-by-name crosswalk.
internalConsistency.disposition: Do not assign dates, exact sampling stations, individual occurrences, counts, abundance, or fishery origin to the listed names.

internalConsistency.issue: The journal calls the article open access but the reviewed article page does not state a machine-readable reuse license; the site carries an all-rights-reserved footer and a copyright-form link.
internalConsistency.disposition: Treat public redistribution and Bangwit publication permission as unresolved; open access is not assumed to grant a reuse license.

interpretation: This is a useful historical Pangasinan river/mangrove source lead, not a current freshwater checklist. The river's salinity and tidal reach are not resolved into separate freshwater, brackish and marine sampling stations.
The article reports 15 fish-name labels, but names are not tied to dates, named stations, vouchers, counts, or distinct primary versus secondary data sources.

Keep the fish-name strings research-only for follow-up taxonomy and source provenance review. Do not add occurrence rows, current-presence claims, abundance, catchability, diet, access, safety, legal status, or river geometry.
No public app projection or source-content redistribution was approved. Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.
nextAction: Seek an independently reusable dated Binmaley or Pangasinan river survey with specimen or per-site provenance; if revisiting this paper, seek the original fish/net data sheets and its specific reuse terms before considering taxonomic normalization or publication.
